## Service — Political PR & Image Building
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/political-pr
Category: Political PR

Answer: Public Pulse Agency runs end-to-end political PR campaigns for Bangladeshi candidates and parties — candidate image building, narrative engineering, opposition research, crisis communication, and a five-phase election execution from pre-campaign positioning to post-election PR. Based in Dhaka, serving constituencies nationwide.

Elections in Bangladesh are won as much in perception as at the polling booth. We help candidates, parties, and political organizations build a coherent public narrative, defend it under pressure, and convert reach into votes.

### Deliverables
- Candidate personal branding — photo, video, biography, public service documentation
- Constituency opinion surveys and local-hero narrative mapping
- Rival/opposition analysis and counter-narrative playbooks
- Five-phase election PR: pre-campaign → mobilization → peak → polling day → post-election
- Crisis communication retainer with 24-hour response SLA
- Debunking, fact-checking, and proactive media outreach

### 5-step process
1. Initial Consultation — Free discovery call to understand the seat, the opposition, and the timeline.
2. Research & Strategy — Constituency survey, rival analysis, audience segmentation, narrative design.
3. Production & Launch — All creative produced in-house; ground-team and digital activated together.
4. Monitor & Optimize — Daily sentiment tracking, A/B narrative tests, rapid pivots when news shifts.
5. Report & Scale — Weekly KPI reports; budget reallocation across constituencies, polling booths, demographics.

### Why us
- **Integrated, not just digital.** Narrative, digital reach, ground-team coordination, and crisis response run as one campaign — under one accountable team.
- **NDA-protected by default.** Every engagement is contracted under NDA. We never work directly competing candidates in the same constituency in the same cycle.
- **24-hour crisis SLA.** When the news cycle turns against you at 11pm, a strategist and a creative are awake and on it by midnight.
- **Bangladesh-native team.** Our strategists, copywriters, and field coordinators are Bangladeshi — not parachuted in. We understand constituency politics here.

### FAQ
**Do you only work with one party?** — No. We work with candidates and parties across the spectrum, but never with directly competing candidates in the same constituency during the same cycle. All engagements are NDA-protected.

**How early should a campaign engage you?** — Ideally 6–9 months before polling. We can run condensed 90-day playbooks but the earlier we start, the cheaper and more effective the narrative work is.

**Is this digital-only, or do you also handle ground operations?** — Both. Our political PR is integrated — narrative, digital reach, ground-team coordination, and crisis response run as one campaign.

## Service — Social Media Management
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/social-media
Category: Social Media

Answer: Public Pulse Agency manages Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and TikTok accounts for Bangladeshi brands — content strategy, weekly posting calendars, Bangla and English community management, paid amplification, and monthly growth reports. We treat social as a sales channel, not a vanity surface.

Facebook still dominates reach in Bangladesh, Instagram drives premium-brand affinity, YouTube is where long-form gets discovered, and TikTok is where the next generation of customers lives. A real social presence ships content on all four — without spreading the team too thin.

### Deliverables
- Quarterly content strategy tied to your sales calendar and offers
- Weekly posting calendar across Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok
- In-house copywriting in Bangla and English, with brand-voice guidelines
- Community management — comment moderation, DM response within 4 working hours
- Monthly performance report: reach, engagement, follower quality, lead attribution
- Crisis response: comment-storm de-escalation and reputation defense

### 5-step process
1. Audit & Strategy — We audit your current accounts, competitor accounts, and the 2–3 angles your audience actually responds to.
2. Content Pipeline Setup — Calendar, brand voice guide, approval workflow, photo and video shoot plan for the next 90 days.
3. Production & Publishing — We ship content weekly across all four platforms; you approve the next week's plan every Friday.
4. Engagement & Amplification — Daily community management, targeted boosting of the top-performing posts, weekly creative iteration.
5. Monthly Review — We meet monthly to review reach, engagement quality, leads generated, and reallocate budget into what's working.

### Why us
- **Bangla-native community management.** Comments and DMs get answered in the language your audience writes in — same day, same tone.
- **One team across all four platforms.** No bouncing between a Meta agency, a YouTube editor and a TikTok freelancer. One brief, one calendar, one set of reports.
- **Sales-channel mindset.** Every post is tagged against a funnel stage. Vanity reach is reported but never celebrated on its own.
- **Crisis-ready.** We carry a comment-storm playbook for hospitality, political and consumer-brand contexts — and we've run it for real clients.

### FAQ
**How many posts per month is included?** — Default plan is 12 Facebook posts, 12 Instagram posts (including Reels), 4 YouTube Shorts and 8 TikToks per month. Volume scales up or down with the retainer. Paid amplification is billed separately as ad spend.

**Can you handle accounts in Bangla, English, or both?** — Both, and code-switched. Our default for consumer brands is Bangla-led with English drops; for B2B and political, mostly English with Bangla quotes where it lands harder.

**Do you bring photo and video, or do we?** — Either works. We can shoot on retainer (as part of our Content Production service), or we can build social calendars on top of your existing photo and video assets.

## Service — Content Production
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/content-production
Category: Content

Answer: Public Pulse Agency produces brand films, social cutdowns, photography, motion graphics, drone footage and UGC content for Bangladeshi brands — shot in Dhaka, Cox's Bazar, Sylhet and on location across the country. Strategy-first scripts, weekly delivery cadence, and content built for the platforms it will actually live on.

Most content fails not at the camera, but at the brief. We start by mapping each video and photo against a sales-funnel stage and a platform, then produce only what fits — fast, in Bangla or English, with brand-safe production standards.

### Deliverables
- Brand films and 60-second sales videos in Bangla and English
- Social cutdowns sized for Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts and Facebook Feed
- Studio and on-location product photography
- Motion graphics and explainer animations
- Drone shoots for hospitality, real estate, events
- UGC content briefs, creator coordination and rights management

### 5-step process
1. Brief & Treatment — We translate your campaign goal into a shot list, mood board, scripts, and a one-page treatment you sign off on.
2. Pre-Production — Location scout, casting, scheduling, permits. We handle the logistics so you don't lose a week to coordination.
3. Shoot Day(s) — Director, DOP, sound and grip on set. Daily rushes shared end-of-day so changes happen before edit, not after.
4. Edit & Versioning — Master edit plus all platform cutdowns produced in one pass — vertical, square, horizontal, with and without captions.
5. Delivery & Iteration — Final files in your preferred formats. We track performance for 30 days and offer one round of creative iteration based on the data.

### Why us
- **Platform-native from the start.** Vertical cutdowns are planned at the storyboard, not crammed into a 16:9 frame afterwards. The same shoot day produces 8–12 deliverables, not one.
- **In-house from script to delivery.** Strategists, scriptwriters, director, DOP, editor and motion designer all under one roof. No subcontracting, no handoff delays.
- **Bangla and English production standards.** Brand-safe Bangla voiceover, subtitle accuracy, font choices that work for both scripts. We get the language right.
- **Built for ad budgets.** We produce versions specifically for paid distribution — hook in 3 seconds, captioned-safe, no audio dependency.

### FAQ
**Can you produce in one day, or do you need weeks?** — A standard one-product social shoot is one day on set, three days in edit — call it ten business days door-to-door. Brand films take three to six weeks. Rush jobs are possible at a 30% premium.

**Do you own the footage or do we?** — You own the final deliverables and the raw footage we shoot. Stock and music we license are licensed to your brand. We retain the right to use the work in our portfolio unless you opt out.

**Where can you shoot?** — Anywhere in Bangladesh. Most-shot locations are Dhaka studios, Cox's Bazar beaches and resorts, Sylhet's tea estates, Bandarban's hill tracts, and Old Dhaka for heritage shoots.

## Service — Paid Ads & Campaigns
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/paid-ads
Category: Paid Ads

Answer: Public Pulse Agency runs paid-media campaigns on Meta, Google and YouTube for Bangladeshi advertisers — full account build, Pixel and Conversion API setup, daily bid and creative optimization, weekly ROAS reports. We work to a return-on-ad-spend target, not impressions, and report in BDT against your CFO's numbers.

Paid media in Bangladesh is cheap if you treat it carelessly and expensive if you don't measure it. We build accounts with proper conversion tracking from day one, kill underperforming creative inside seven days, and double down on what produces revenue — not what produces likes.

### Deliverables
- Meta Ads (Facebook + Instagram): full account setup, audience design, creative testing
- Google Ads: Search, Display, Performance Max, YouTube — keyword and bid management
- Conversion tracking: Meta Pixel + Conversion API, GA4, Google Ads conversions, server-side wherever possible
- Daily account optimization with documented changes — never silent edits
- Weekly ROAS reports in BDT, monthly strategy review meeting
- Landing-page conversion audits and recommendations

### 5-step process
1. Account & Tracking Audit — We audit your existing accounts and conversion tracking — most accounts we inherit have leaky measurement, and we fix it first.
2. Strategy & Build — Funnel design, audience mapping, creative brief, naming conventions, budget split across channels and campaign stages.
3. Creative Production & Launch — We brief and ship at least 6 creatives per channel before launch — no campaign goes live with one ad.
4. Daily Optimization — Daily bid and budget adjustments; weekly creative refresh; underperformers killed inside seven days.
5. Weekly Report & Reallocation — Friday report: spend, conversions, CPA, ROAS by campaign. Monday call: reallocate budget into the top quartile.

### Why us
- **Built for BDT budgets.** We tune for accounts spending ৳50,000–৳20,00,000/month — not 10x that. Tactics, bid strategies and creative volume match real Bangladeshi budgets.
- **Conversion API set up properly.** iOS tracking loss kills most agency reporting. We set up server-side Conversion API and Enhanced Conversions before launch, not after.
- **No silent edits.** Every change to your account is logged with timestamp, rationale and predicted impact. You can audit our work line-by-line.
- **We sit on your side of the table.** We name and shame our own losing creative in reports. Honesty about what's not working is how we get to what does.

### FAQ
**What's a typical monthly ad spend you work with?** — Most clients spend between ৳1,00,000 and ৳10,00,000/month across Meta and Google combined. We can start lower for testing — ৳50,000/month is enough to learn what works.

**Do you charge a flat fee or a percentage of ad spend?** — Both options. Flat retainers start at ৳60,000/month for one channel. Percentage-of-spend is 12–18% depending on volume — drops as your spend grows so the math always favors scaling.

**How fast will I see ROAS results?** — Paid social usually shows reliable signal at 14 days; paid search at 7. Real optimization — killing losers and scaling winners — takes 30–60 days. Don't judge a campaign on its first week.

## Service — Hospitality Marketing
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/hospitality
Category: Hospitality

Answer: Public Pulse Agency markets Bangladeshi resorts, hotels and restaurants — Cox's Bazar to Sylhet, Dhaka to Chittagong. OTA listing optimization, Google Business Profile, food-delivery platform management, video tours, and paid campaigns that fill rooms and tables on the calendar dates that need filling.

Hospitality in Bangladesh is a calendar business — Eid weeks, the winter season for Cox's Bazar, the monsoon dip for Sylhet. We plan campaigns against your occupancy and cover-count targets by week, not by quarter, and the metric is bookings and orders — not reach.

### Deliverables
- OTA optimization: Booking.com, Agoda, GoZayaan, Expedia — listings, photos, pricing, response time
- Google Business Profile: photos, hours, posts, review responses, Q&A management
- Food-delivery platforms: Foodpanda, Pathao Food — menu, photography, ranking optimization
- Resort and restaurant video tours (drone + interior + chef's table)
- Paid campaigns aimed at occupancy or covers, with day-parted budget
- Weekly review-management: respond to every Google, Facebook and OTA review within 24 hours

### 5-step process
1. Property Audit — Walk the property (in person or via video). Audit current OTAs, GBP, social, photos, reviews and price positioning vs the comp set.
2. Calendar Planning — Map your occupancy or cover-count goals against your real calendar — Eid, winter season, monsoon dip, school holidays, conference weeks.
3. Asset & Listing Buildout — Refresh photos, write listings, set pricing rules, build the menu page. Get the foundations indexable and clickable.
4. Campaign Activation — Paid campaigns aimed at the weeks that need filling. Always-on local SEO and review management running underneath.
5. Weekly Occupancy Review — Friday call: actual vs planned occupancy or covers, what's pacing low, where we shift spend for the coming week.

### Why us
- **We've worked the Cox's Bazar season.** We know the winter pricing curve, the OTA dynamics, the resort comp set, and which weeks panic-booking pays off.
- **Bangla + English review responses.** Reviews answered in the guest's language, in your brand voice, within 24 hours — by humans, not templates.
- **Calendar-led campaigns.** Spend is timed to fill the specific weeks that aren't selling, not flat-lined across the month for vanity reach.
- **Hospitality-trained creative team.** Our drone operators, food photographers and video editors have shot resorts, restaurants and hotels — not just learned on yours.

### FAQ
**Do you only work with luxury properties?** — No. We work across mid-market and luxury — Cox's Bazar resorts at ৳5,000–৳25,000/night, Dhaka restaurants from neighborhood cafés to fine-dining, and boutique hotels in Sylhet and Bandarban.

**What's the typical engagement length?** — Twelve months is the standard — hospitality calendars are seasonal and a six-month engagement misses too many cycles. We do offer 90-day intensives to fix a specific season.

**Do you handle bookings or just marketing?** — Marketing only. We drive demand to your existing booking flow (OTA, direct site, phone, WhatsApp). We can recommend booking-engine fixes — implementation goes through our SEO & Website team.

## Service — Brand Building & Design
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/brand-building
Category: Branding

Answer: Public Pulse Agency builds brand identities for Bangladeshi startups and rebrands for established businesses — naming, logo, visual identity, packaging, brand voice guidelines, and a positioning map against your real competitors. The output is a brand book your team can actually apply, not a moodboard that lives in a Drive folder.

A brand is the sum of every visual and verbal cue your customer sees, repeated until it becomes recognizable. We design those cues deliberately — and ship a brand book that makes them reproducible by anyone on your team, not just by us.

### Deliverables
- Brand discovery: customer interviews, founder interviews, competitor positioning analysis
- Naming (for new brands or sub-brands): shortlist, trademark check, domain availability
- Logo system: primary mark, secondary mark, monogram, lockups, light/dark variants
- Visual identity: color palette, typography, photography style, iconography, illustration system
- Packaging design (consumer goods, FMCG, hospitality collateral)
- Brand voice & messaging guidelines: tone, taglines, do/don't language examples
- Brand book PDF + Figma library + asset zip — versioned and handover-ready

### 5-step process
1. Discovery Workshop — Two-hour workshop with founders. We surface the audience, the competition, the cultural cues, and the truth-of-the-brand we're going to build around.
2. Strategic Positioning — Positioning statement, brand pillars, voice principles. We get sign-off on words before pixels — because brands fail at the words.
3. Identity Design — Logo, palette, type, photography. Two to three rounds of concepts, narrowed and refined. Always tested against real applications, not isolated on a white slide.
4. System & Application — Apply the identity to your real touchpoints — packaging, social, signage, deck templates, email. The brand book is built from real examples.
5. Handover & Training — Brand book delivered with a 60-minute team training so your in-house marketers can apply the system without our help.

### Why us
- **Built for application, not for awards.** We design what your team can apply at 11pm on a Friday. Brand books that survive contact with real production briefs.
- **Bangladesh-aware design.** We know which Latin typefaces pair well with Bangla, which colors carry political connotations, and which packaging conventions work for FMCG here.
- **Founders in the room.** Strategy decisions get made with the founder present — not relayed through a junior account manager. Faster decisions, fewer rebriefs.
- **Figma library handover.** You leave with a working Figma library (components, variables, swatches) — not just a PDF. Your in-house designer can keep building.

### FAQ
**How long does a full brand build take?** — Eight to twelve weeks for a new brand from scratch (naming + identity + brand book). Six to eight weeks for an identity refresh on an existing brand. Rushed five-week sprints are possible at a 25% premium.

**Do you do naming, or do we bring the name?** — Both. Naming adds two to three weeks (legal and domain checks take real time). If you bring the name, we validate it for trademark conflict and audience perception before designing around it.

**What if we need a logo refresh, not a full rebrand?** — We offer logo-refresh-only engagements — typically four to six weeks, smaller fee. Useful when the strategy is solid but the visual identity has aged out.

## Service — SEO & Website Development
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/seo-website
Category: SEO

Answer: Public Pulse Agency runs SEO and builds websites for Bangladeshi businesses — local SEO, technical SEO, on-page optimization, schema markup, and conversion-focused website builds in Next.js or WordPress. We aim for traffic that converts, not traffic that bounces, and we measure rankings against the queries your customers actually type.

SEO without a fast, well-structured website is wasted; a website without SEO is invisible. We do both, in sequence — the website is built to rank from day one, and the SEO program is built around what the website is actually good at.

### Deliverables
- Technical SEO audit: crawlability, indexability, Core Web Vitals, schema
- On-page SEO: titles, meta descriptions, header structure, internal linking, image optimization
- Local SEO: Google Business Profile setup, citation cleanup, review-generation flow
- Schema markup: Organization, LocalBusiness, Article, Service, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList
- Website development: Next.js or WordPress, mobile-first, accessibility-aware, fast
- Monthly rankings, traffic and conversion reports
- Content briefs for blog and service pages (writing is a separate line item if you need it)

### 5-step process
1. Audit — Full technical and on-page audit of your existing site, plus a keyword opportunity report for the next 12 months.
2. Fix & Build — Address technical debt, ship missing schema, rebuild slow pages. Or — if the site can't be saved — design and build a new one.
3. Content & Internal Linking — Brief in pillar pages, fix orphan pages, build the internal-link graph between services, blog and case studies.
4. Local SEO Activation — Google Business Profile fully optimized, citations cleaned up across local directories, review-generation flow live.
5. Monthly Reporting — Rankings, organic traffic, conversion rate, Core Web Vitals — and what we shipped this month against last month's plan.

### Why us
- **We build the site we'll have to rank.** When SEO and dev are the same team, no one can blame the other for slow pages or missing schema. Accountability is built in.
- **Schema and AEO from day one.** Article, Service, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList — done at build time, not bolted on later. Your pages are eligible for AI Overviews, Bing Copilot and ChatGPT citations.
- **Core Web Vitals as a discipline.** LCP under 2.5s, CLS under 0.1, INP under 200ms — measured weekly, fixed weekly. No 'launched and forgot it' performance.
- **We rank our own site for SEO Bangladesh.** If you can't see us in the Google results that brought you here, fire us. Eat-your-own-dog-food is the only credible SEO pitch.

### FAQ
**How long until SEO produces real traffic?** — New domains: 6–12 months before organic traffic becomes a meaningful channel. Established domains we're fixing: 60–90 days for initial wins, 6 months for a defensible ranking position.

**Next.js or WordPress — which should we choose?** — Next.js for marketing sites you'll grow into programmatic SEO, complex pricing pages, or SaaS dashboards. WordPress when an in-house non-technical team will publish blog posts and edit pages weekly. We're fluent in both.

**Do you guarantee a #1 ranking?** — No reputable SEO does. We guarantee the work — audit, fixes, content, schema, link building, monthly reports — and a clear forecast of expected traffic against keyword difficulty. Anyone promising rank #1 is selling you a refund opportunity.

## Service — Analytics & Performance Reporting
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/analytics-reporting
Category: Analytics

Answer: Public Pulse Agency sets up GA4, Google Tag Manager, Meta Pixel and Conversion API for Bangladeshi advertisers, then builds Looker Studio dashboards that surface marketing ROI in BDT against revenue. Monthly reports that pass an audit — and that your CFO will actually read instead of forwarding to the marketing team for translation.

Marketing reports usually answer the wrong question. Yours should answer one thing: did this month's spend produce more revenue than it cost? Our analytics stack is built backwards from that question.

### Deliverables
- GA4 setup or migration from Universal Analytics, with proper event schema
- Google Tag Manager: container build, naming conventions, version control
- Meta Pixel + Conversion API (server-side via Cloudflare Worker or your backend)
- Google Ads conversions, Enhanced Conversions, offline conversion imports
- Looker Studio dashboards: campaign-level, channel-level, executive-level
- Monthly ROI report in BDT with attribution model documented
- Quarterly attribution review — which channels actually drove revenue, which got false credit

### 5-step process
1. Stack Audit — We inventory every tracking pixel, every Tag Manager container, every GA4 property — and document what's broken, duplicated or sending bad data.
2. Rebuild & Validate — Clean GTM container, GA4 event schema, server-side Meta Conversion API, Google Ads Enhanced Conversions. We validate every event with real test transactions before signing off.
3. Dashboard Build — Looker Studio dashboards at three altitudes — campaign-detail for the buyer, channel-summary for the marketing lead, ROI-only for the CFO.
4. Monthly Reporting Cadence — Monthly PDF report + 30-min review call. Spend, conversions, CPA, ROAS, contribution-margin if we have the data.
5. Quarterly Attribution Review — Every 90 days we re-examine which channels truly drove revenue using multi-touch attribution — and reallocate next quarter's budget accordingly.

### Why us
- **Server-side first.** iOS tracking loss is real. We deploy Conversion API server-side from day one, recovering 20–40% of conversion signal most agencies leave on the table.
- **BDT-native reporting.** Reports are in taka, against your actual revenue, against your actual COGS where available — not in dollars with a vague 'ROAS' figure.
- **Auditable container.** Our GTM containers are version-controlled with clear naming. You can hand them to another agency in 30 minutes if you ever need to — and that fact alone is why most clients stay.
- **We say no to vanity dashboards.** If a metric won't change a decision, it doesn't go on the dashboard. Pages that nobody reads are debt, not value.

### FAQ
**We're still on Universal Analytics — can you migrate us?** — Yes. GA4 migration is a 3–4 week project. We rebuild the event schema, set up GTM properly, validate against your old data, and keep both systems live during the transition.

**How much does the analytics service cost?** — Setup is a one-time project (typically ৳1,50,000–৳4,00,000 depending on stack complexity). Monthly reporting + maintenance retainer starts at ৳35,000/month and scales with the number of channels and properties.

**Do you replace our marketing team, or work with them?** — We work with them. Our job is to give the marketing team a trustworthy measurement layer so their decisions get made on real data — not to take over campaign execution unless that's also in scope.

## Service — Influencer & KOL Marketing
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/influencer-marketing
Category: Influencer

Answer: Public Pulse Agency runs influencer and KOL campaigns across Bangladesh — discovery from a vetted creator pool, tier strategy from nano to macro, contracts and briefs, FTC-compliant disclosure, and tracked performance with verified results. We treat influencer as a measurable acquisition channel, not a goodwill spend.

Most influencer campaigns are run on vibes — a creator with a big follower count, a one-off post, no measurement, no contract that protects either side. We run them like paid media: target customer profile, tracked link or promo code, post-campaign performance report.

### Deliverables
- Creator discovery from our vetted Bangladesh pool — nano (1K–10K), micro (10K–100K), mid (100K–1M), macro (1M+)
- Audience-quality verification: bot detection, follower demographic match, engagement-rate sanity check
- Brief writing, content guidelines, brand-safety review of every post before publishing
- Contracts: deliverables, exclusivity windows, usage rights, FTC-compliant disclosure clauses
- Tracking: UTM-tagged links, unique promo codes, conversion attribution per creator
- Post-campaign report: reach, engagement, attributed sales, cost-per-acquired-customer per creator
- Long-term ambassador programs and retainer agreements

### 5-step process
1. Brief & Target Profile — We translate your campaign goal into a target customer profile, a content brief, and the creator tiers that match the budget.
2. Creator Shortlist — We pull 8–15 verified creators per campaign — audience demographic match, engagement-rate sanity, prior brand work, no bot inflation.
3. Negotiation & Contracting — We negotiate rates, lock deliverables, sign contracts with exclusivity windows and usage rights. Disclosure language is contractually required.
4. Production & Publishing — Brief sent, draft reviewed, brand-safety check before live. Posting schedule coordinated for campaign-window impact.
5. Tracking & Reporting — UTM links and promo codes tagged per creator. Post-campaign report shows reach, engagement, attributed conversions and CPA per creator — we can name who actually drove sales.

### Why us
- **Vetted creator pool.** Our creator list is screened for bot inflation, real engagement, audience demographic and prior brand-safety incidents. No surprises after the contract is signed.
- **Per-creator attribution.** Promo codes and UTM links are mandatory in our briefs. You see which creator drove orders, not just which creator posted — and renew or retire creators on that data.
- **Contracts that actually protect you.** Exclusivity windows, usage rights, takedown rights for off-brand posts, FTC-compliant disclosure. Real legal-grade contracts, not Google Doc handshakes.
- **Bangladesh-native relationships.** We work in BDT, we know the creator landscape, and we have direct relationships with most top-100 Bangladesh creators — meaning faster yes/no, fairer rates, and reliable delivery.

### FAQ
**What's a realistic budget for an influencer campaign in Bangladesh?** — Nano-creator (1K–10K followers) campaigns start at ৳5,000–৳15,000 per post. Micro (10K–100K) typically ৳15,000–৳60,000. Mid (100K–1M) ৳60,000–৳3,00,000. Macro (1M+) is ৳3,00,000+ and often a separate negotiation per post.

**How do you measure ROI when influencers don't drive a clickable link?** — Three signals stacked: unique promo codes (works for e-commerce), UTM links in bio (works when the platform allows), and pre/post lift studies in branded search (works for awareness campaigns). We always set at least two of the three before launch.

**Will the creator disclose the partnership?** — Always. Our contracts require platform-compliant disclosure (Meta's branded content tool, #ad or #sponsored). It protects your brand from regulatory action and platform takedowns — and the data shows disclosed posts perform within 5% of undisclosed ones, so there's no downside.

## Location — Dhaka (Dhaka Division)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/locations/dhaka
Coordinates: 23.8103, 90.4125  ·  Population: 10M+

# Glossary

---

## Glossary — Answer Block (উত্তর ব্লক)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/answer-block
Area: SEO

**Definition:** A short 40–60 word self-contained answer placed at the top of a long-form page, designed for AI engines (Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity) to lift verbatim.

Answer blocks are the most important AEO/GEO surface on a content page. They give AI engines a complete, citable answer in the page's first viewport so the engine doesn't synthesize one from elsewhere. Public Pulse renders every long-form page's answer block inside a <section class='answer-block' data-speakable> wrapper so the Article JSON-LD's `speakable` cssSelector can target it.

---

## Glossary — AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) (উত্তর ইঞ্জিন অপ্টিমাইজেশন)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/aeo
Area: SEO

**Definition:** Optimizing a page so AI-driven answer engines — Google AI Overviews, Bing Copilot, voice assistants — cite it as the source for direct answers.

AEO is the second-generation evolution of SEO. The win-state is no longer the blue link click; it's the citation inside an AI-generated answer. AEO works by combining clear answer-first prose (see Answer Block), explicit JSON-LD with the right @type for the question (FAQPage, HowTo, DefinedTerm), and being the most factually accurate source in your domain so the engine prefers you.

---

## Glossary — GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) (জেনারেটিভ ইঞ্জিন অপ্টিমাইজেশন)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/geo
Area: SEO

**Definition:** Optimizing a page so generative engines (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini) ground their answers in your content when a user asks a related question.

GEO is what happens after AEO: the engine isn't just citing you, it's grounding its entire generated answer in your prose. The unlock is making sure your content is indexable by the LLM crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot — see robots.txt) AND making the content easy to ground in (specific dated facts, plain-language explainers, glossary cross-links).

---

## Glossary — FAQPage Schema (FAQPage স্কিমা)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/faqpage-schema
Area: SEO

**Definition:** A schema.org JSON-LD type that marks up a page's FAQ section, telling search engines exactly which question + answer pairs to consider for rich snippets and AI citations.

Every long-form Public Pulse page emits FAQPage JSON-LD with at least 3 Question + Answer pairs (a HARD gate in the quality pipeline). The questions should match how real users phrase their queries — short, conversational, in their language — not how an SEO team would phrase a keyword.

---

## Glossary — JSON-LD Schema (JSON-LD স্কিমা)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/schema-jsonld
Area: SEO

**Definition:** Structured data embedded in a <script type='application/ld+json'> tag, describing the page's entities (Service, Article, Organization, FAQPage, etc.) for machines.

Public Pulse uses typed builders in src/lib/schema.ts so every page emits valid JSON-LD with stable @id URIs that cross-reference Organization. Hand-rolling JSON-LD is banned because field omissions silently kill rich-result eligibility.

---

## Glossary — llms.txt (llms.txt)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/llms-txt
Area: SEO

**Definition:** A plain-text file at /llms.txt that gives AI engines a curated, link-rich summary of the site to ground from — analogous to robots.txt for crawlers.

llms.txt follows the llmstxt.org convention. Public Pulse publishes both /llms.txt (curated index) and /llms-full.txt (concatenated full-text). Both serve HTTP 200 directly, never redirects.

---

## Glossary — robots.txt (robots.txt)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/robots-txt
Area: SEO

**Definition:** A plain-text file at /robots.txt that tells crawlers which paths they're allowed to fetch.

Public Pulse's robots.txt explicitly allows GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and Bingbot for the public site, and explicitly disallows /manage and /api/auth. The AI-crawler allow-list is intentional — we want our pages cited in AI answers.

---

## Glossary — Speakable (স্পিকেবল)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/speakable
Area: SEO

**Definition:** A schema.org property on Article that tells voice assistants (Google Assistant, Alexa) which CSS selector contains the spoken-aloud answer.

Public Pulse Article schema sets `speakable.cssSelector: ['.answer-block']` so the assistant reads our 40–60 word answer block, not random body copy. Don't rename the .answer-block class without updating src/lib/schema.ts.

---

## Glossary — Political PR (রাজনৈতিক জনসংযোগ)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/political-pr
Area: Political PR

**Definition:** Public communications strategy for political candidates, parties, and elected officials — candidate image-building, narrative engineering, opposition research, crisis communications.

In Bangladesh, political PR runs on a five-phase election cycle: pre-campaign positioning, ground research, narrative launch, polling-day execution, post-election PR. Public Pulse runs all five.

---

## Glossary — Narrative Engineering (ন্যারেটিভ ইঞ্জিনিয়ারিং)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/narrative-engineering
Area: Political PR

**Definition:** The deliberate construction of a campaign's core message, tested against constituency demographics and refined for sticking power.

A narrative isn't a slogan. It's a story arc — what the candidate stands for, what they're against, what changes if they win — engineered to be retold by voters in their own words. We test narratives in field interviews before committing media spend.

---

## Glossary — Opposition Research (অপজিশন রিসার্চ)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/opposition-research
Area: Political PR

**Definition:** Systematic intelligence-gathering on an opponent's record, statements, vulnerabilities, and likely lines of attack — used both to anticipate threats and to brief the candidate's own counter-messaging.

Done responsibly: published statements, public records, verifiable claims. Used to prepare the candidate, NOT to seed disinformation. Public Pulse maintains an internal ethics standard on what we publish vs what we only brief the candidate on.

---

## Glossary — Meta Conversions API (CAPI) (মেটা কনভার্সন এপিআই)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/meta-conversions-api
Area: Paid Media

**Definition:** Server-to-server event tracking from your site/CRM to Meta's ad platform, used to recover conversion signal lost to iOS ATT and ad blockers.

Browser-side Meta Pixel firing drops 30–50%+ of events post-iOS-14.5. CAPI sends the same events from your server so Meta's bidding has a more complete signal. Public Pulse implements both pixel + CAPI on every e-commerce build.

---

## Glossary — ROAS (Return on Ad Spend) (বিজ্ঞাপন ব্যয়ের উপর রিটার্ন)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/roas
Area: Paid Media

**Definition:** Revenue generated for every BDT spent on advertising. A ROAS of 4× means BDT 4 of revenue per BDT 1 of ad spend.

ROAS is the headline metric for e-commerce paid media. The trap: it's a vanity metric in isolation — high ROAS with declining new-customer share is a slow death. Public Pulse reports ROAS alongside new-vs-returning split and contribution-margin ROAS (revenue minus COGS minus ad spend).

---

## Glossary — CTR (Click-Through Rate) (ক্লিক-থ্রু রেট)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/ctr
Area: Paid Media

**Definition:** The fraction of ad impressions that became clicks. Calculated as clicks ÷ impressions × 100.

Benchmark CTRs vary wildly by placement: a 1% CTR on Meta feed is industry-average; the same on a search ad is poor. CTR matters as a creative-quality signal but isn't the goal — conversion rate downstream is.

---

## Glossary — IndexNow (ইনডেক্সনাও)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/indexnow
Area: SEO

**Definition:** An open protocol that lets a site instantly notify participating search engines (Bing, Yandex, Seznam) when a URL is published, updated, or deleted — bypassing crawl-budget delays.

Public Pulse pings IndexNow on every /manage publish action with the affected URLs. Google does not participate but the major Bing-backed engines do. Our key file lives at /indexnow-key.txt.

---

## Glossary — Speakable Schema (স্পিকেবল স্কিমা)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/speakable-schema
Area: SEO

**Definition:** The schema.org SpeakableSpecification — placed on Article or WebPage JSON-LD with a cssSelector that points voice assistants at the prose they should read aloud as the answer.

Speakable schema is the voice-assistant cousin of FAQPage. Google Assistant and Alexa pick the cssSelector you provide (Public Pulse uses ['.answer-block']) and read it verbatim. The selector should target a 40–60 word self-contained answer; longer passages get truncated mid-sentence on the device. We render every long-form page's answer block inside <section class='answer-block' data-speakable> so the selector matches deterministically.

---

## Glossary — First-Party Data (ফার্স্ট-পার্টি ডেটা)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/first-party-data
Area: Analytics

**Definition:** Customer data the business collected directly — from its own site, app, CRM, point-of-sale or call centre — as opposed to third-party data bought from data brokers or rented from ad platforms.

First-party data is the strategic asset for Bangladeshi brands as Meta and Google narrow third-party signal (iOS ATT, third-party cookie deprecation). The unlock is a clean Customer ID linked across web, Bkash/Nagad transactions, and WhatsApp inbox so you can build audiences and lookalikes inside Meta CAPI / Google Enhanced Conversions without leaking PII. Public Pulse implements first-party data layers as the foundation of every analytics rebuild.

---

## Glossary — Attribution Window (অ্যাট্রিবিউশন উইন্ডো)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/attribution-window
Area: Analytics

**Definition:** The look-back period an ad platform credits an ad with a conversion — e.g. a 7-day-click 1-day-view window means Meta will count a purchase as the ad's outcome if it happens within 7 days of a click or 1 day of a view.

Attribution windows are the single most over-looked lever in Bangladeshi paid media reporting. Meta defaults to 7-day-click; a hospitality brand selling 30-day-booking-window resorts is invisible under that default. Public Pulse audits attribution windows before every reporting setup and reconciles to first-party booking data so ROAS reflects reality, not the platform's default look-back. Mixing windows across channels — Google's data-driven model vs Meta's 7-day-click — produces double-counting at the campaign-mix level; we normalize.

---

## Glossary — Engagement Rate (এনগেজমেন্ট রেট)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/engagement-rate
Area: Digital Marketing

**Definition:** The fraction of an audience that interacted with a piece of content — likes, comments, shares, saves, click-throughs — usually expressed as engagements ÷ reach × 100.

Engagement rate is the dominant proxy metric on Bangladeshi Facebook and Instagram for organic content health. Healthy benchmarks: 2–5% on Facebook, 3–6% on Instagram for branded posts in the BD market; influencer rates run higher (5–12%). The trap is using ER alone to evaluate paid creative — paid CTAs depress ER mechanically while driving the actual KPI. Public Pulse separates organic ER (community signal) from paid CTR / conversion rate (commercial signal) in every monthly report.

---

## Glossary — Core Web Vitals (কোর ওয়েব ভাইটালস)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/core-web-vitals
Area: SEO

**Definition:** Google's three page-experience metrics — LCP (largest contentful paint, load speed), INP (interaction to next paint, responsiveness), and CLS (cumulative layout shift, visual stability) — used as a ranking signal and surfaced in Search Console.

Core Web Vitals matter twice in Bangladesh: as a ranking signal Google demonstrably uses, and as a UX-on-3G signal that dominates conversion for hospitality, real estate, and e-commerce sites where buyers research on phones over patchy networks. Pass-thresholds: LCP ≤ 2.5s, INP ≤ 200ms, CLS ≤ 0.1. Public Pulse's standard build (Next.js + OpenNext + CloudFront with AVIF/WebP image responses) ships green CWV on a Bangladeshi 4G device out of the box; the failure mode is usually heavy embeds added later (chat widgets, slow Tag Manager containers).

---

## Glossary — Conversion API (কনভার্সন এপিআই)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/conversion-api
Area: Paid Media

**Definition:** A server-to-server event protocol — Meta's Conversions API, Google's Enhanced Conversions, TikTok's Events API — that sends conversion data directly from the brand's server to the ad platform, bypassing browser tracking that iOS ATT and ad blockers degrade.

Conversion API is one of two technical lifts every Bangladeshi e-commerce stack must do post-iOS-14.5 (the other is first-party data). Server-side events restore 30–50% of the conversion signal lost from browser-side pixels. Public Pulse implements Meta CAPI alongside the browser pixel (dedup by event_id), so the platform sees both signals and Meta's bidding has clean attribution. Without CAPI, Meta's algorithm optimizes against a partial dataset and CPA inflates 20–40% over a 6-month decay curve.

---

## Glossary — Boosted Post (বুস্টেড পোস্ট)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/boosted-post
Area: Paid Media

**Definition:** Paying to extend the reach of an existing Facebook or Instagram post. It is the simplest Meta ad — but when the content is political, a boosted post still requires ad authorization and a “Paid for by” disclaimer.

Boosting is where almost every Bangladeshi candidate starts, because it is one tap from a page post. It is fast and blunt: limited targeting, one creative, no message testing, no frequency control. It works to amplify a moment that is already resonating — a rally clip, a local win — but it does not carry a message through a constituency the way an Ads Manager campaign does. Crucially, boosting political content without completing Meta’s authorization and disclaimer is a policy violation that gets ads rejected and pages restricted. Public Pulse boosts only from authorized, disclaimed accounts, and only when a boost is genuinely the right tool.

---

## Glossary — Ad Authorization (বিজ্ঞাপন অনুমোদন)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/ad-authorization
Area: Paid Media

**Definition:** Meta’s identity- and location-verification that an advertiser must complete before running ads about elections, politics, or social issues. Without it, political ads are rejected.

Before a single political ad runs, Meta requires the advertiser to confirm a verified identity and an in-country location, and to register who is paying. In Bangladesh this step is the one most local operators skip — and it is exactly why their ads get pulled at the worst moment, often in the final week. Authorization can take days, so Public Pulse completes it per account ahead of the campaign, not at launch. It is the gate the entire operation depends on: no authorization, no compliant reach.

---

## Glossary — “Paid for by” Disclaimer (“যার অর্থায়নে” ঘোষণা)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/paid-for-by-disclaimer
Area: Paid Media

**Definition:** The mandatory label on every political ad naming who paid for it. Registered once on an authorized account, it then appears on every ad the campaign runs.

Meta requires political ads to carry a visible disclaimer stating who paid. It is registered once during authorization and applied automatically to every ad. The disclaimer is not a formality — it is what keeps a campaign on the right side of both Meta’s rules and public scrutiny, and it feeds the public Ad Library where anyone can see what a candidate is running. Public Pulse treats the disclaimer as a discipline: if a message could not stand next to the name of who paid for it, it does not run.

---

## Glossary — Special Ad Category (বিশেষ বিজ্ঞাপন শ্রেণি)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/special-ad-category
Area: Paid Media

**Definition:** Meta’s restricted category for political, electoral, and social-issue ads that limits targeting — no narrowing by age, gender, or detailed personal traits the way commercial ads allow.

When an ad is classified as political or social-issue, Meta places it in a Special Ad Category and strips away much of the fine-grained targeting available to commercial advertisers. You cannot narrow by detailed demographics or many interest traits. That sounds like a handicap; in practice it forces the discipline that actually wins constituencies — building reach on geography and legitimate affinity. Public Pulse designs every political campaign to perform inside these limits from the start, rather than fighting them, so nothing is rejected on review.

---

## Glossary — Constituency Targeting (আসনভিত্তিক টার্গেটিং)
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/constituency-targeting
Area: Paid Media

**Definition:** Focusing paid Facebook reach on a specific electoral seat using Meta’s geography and affinity layers, within Special Ad Category limits — targeting the voters who decide the margin, not vanity reach.

A national ad set wastes most of a candidate’s budget on people who cannot vote for them. Constituency targeting tunes the location radius to union, ward, and upazila lines and weights spend toward the pockets that decide the seat. Because political ads sit in the Special Ad Category, this is built on geography and legitimate affinity rather than protected traits. In Bangladesh it also means designing for a mobile, data-light, Bangla-first electorate. Public Pulse targets the seat, tracks reach and frequency against it, and reallocates daily toward the wards that move.

---

# Guides

---

## Guide (HowTo) — How to run a Facebook ad campaign for a Bangladesh constituency election
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/guides/facebook-campaign-bd-election
Estimated time: 2h30m
Tools: Meta Ads Manager, Meta Business Suite, Meta Conversions API, Meta Ad Library

Answer: Before anything else, complete Meta ad authorization (identity + location) and register the “Paid for by” disclaimer — political ads are rejected without them. Then pin a geo-radius to the constituency, run Bangla-first creative within Special Ad Category limits, back it with CAPI, and heavy-weight budget in the final 14 days. Full offer: /political-facebook-ads-bangladesh.

Step-by-step playbook for setting up a constituency-targeted Meta ads campaign for a Bangladeshi political candidate — from audience build to compliance to budget pacing.

### Prerequisites
- Verified Meta Business Page for the candidate
- Ability to complete Meta political-ad authorization (ID + in-country location)
- Ad account with BDT payment method on file
- Constituency boundary coordinates (lat/lng polygon)

### Steps
1. **Authorize the ad account + register the “Paid for by” disclaimer** — Before any spend: complete Meta’s political-ad authorization (verified identity + in-country location) and register the disclaimer naming who pays. This can take days — do it early, because unauthorized political ads are rejected and pages get restricted. See /political-facebook-ads-bangladesh for the full compliance regime.

2. **Build the constituency-pinned audience** — In Meta Ads Manager → Audiences → Create a custom audience with a geo-radius drawn over the constituency. Layer in age 18+ and language=Bangla. Save this audience by name — you'll reuse it for every ad in the cycle.

3. **Set up Conversions API (CAPI) for the campaign site** — Server-side event tracking from the candidate's microsite to Meta — recovers signal lost to iOS ATT and ad blockers, which is critical during a campaign's final week when click-noise spikes.

4. **Author Bangla-first creative (image + video variants)** — Test 3 image and 2 video variants on a BDT 5,000 micro-budget. Winning variants by reach + CTR move to the main campaign.

5. **Configure budget pacing for the cycle** — Heavy-weight the final 14 days. Recommended split: 20% pre-narrative (T-60 to T-30), 30% sustained (T-30 to T-14), 50% closing window (T-14 to polling day).

6. **Stay inside Special Ad Category + Ad Library, then archive** — Keep every ad within Meta's Special Ad Category — no protected-trait targeting — and remember all political ads are archived in Meta's public Ad Library for years, so write and target assuming full visibility. Save all creative, targeting, and spend to a candidate archive; BD has no BCRA-equivalent disclosure yet, but expect a request from the EC — have it ready.

---

## Guide (HowTo) — Set up Meta Conversions API for a Bangladesh e-commerce site
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/guides/meta-conversions-api-setup
Estimated time: 1h
Tools: Meta Events Manager, Meta Business Suite, Server-side webhook

Answer: Meta Conversions API is server-to-server event tracking from your site to Meta — recovering the 30–50% of conversion signal that browser pixels lose to iOS ATT and ad blockers. Setup is one-time, takes about an hour, and is essential for Bangladesh e-commerce where COD pushes the last-mile event off-site entirely.

Recover the 30–50% of conversion signal lost to iOS ATT and ad blockers. Walkthrough of server-side event tracking via Meta CAPI on a Next.js / Shopify / WooCommerce stack.

### Prerequisites
- Existing Meta Pixel installed
- Server-side language access (Node, PHP, Python — any HTTP-capable runtime)
- Access token from Meta Events Manager

### Steps
1. **Generate a Conversions API access token** — Meta Events Manager → Data Sources → your pixel → Settings → Set up manually → Generate access token. Store it in your server secrets (NEVER in client code).

2. **Emit events server-side from purchase / lead routes** — POST /v18.0/{pixel_id}/events with the same event_name + event_id you use client-side. Matching event_ids let Meta dedupe between browser + server events.

3. **Hash all PII before sending** — Email, phone, name fields must be SHA-256 hashed before sending. Meta's docs show the exact normalization (lowercase email, strip whitespace, etc.) — follow it exactly.

4. **Verify event match quality in Events Manager** — Wait 24 hours, then check Events Manager → Overview → Event Match Quality. Target ≥ 7.0; below 5.0 means your PII isn't matching Meta's user records.

5. **Test before going live** — Use Meta's Test Events feature to fire a sample event and confirm it lands. Don't enable CAPI ads-side optimization until match quality is verified.

---

## Guide (HowTo) — Add IndexNow to your publish pipeline
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/guides/indexnow-publish-pipeline
Estimated time: 30m
Tools: A reachable HTTP server, A UUID-like 8-128 char key

Answer: IndexNow is an open protocol that lets your site instantly notify Bing, Yandex and consortium engines when URLs publish, update, or delete. Setup is one key file at /indexnow-key.txt plus a single HTTP POST on every publish. Google doesn't participate but Bing-backed search covers most of the rest.

Notify Bing, Yandex and other consortium engines the instant a page goes live — bypass crawl-budget delays for time-sensitive content (election PR, breaking news, product launches).

### Prerequisites
- Ability to host a static text file on your site root
- A publish hook in your CMS

### Steps
1. **Generate and host the key file** — Create a random 8-128 char alphanumeric key. Host it at /indexnow-key.txt with the key as the only content. The filename must match the key.

2. **POST the changed URL on every publish** — POST https://api.indexnow.org/indexnow with body { host, key, keyLocation, urlList }. Send the list of URLs that just published, updated or were deleted.

3. **Confirm acceptance** — HTTP 200 = accepted. 422 = key/keyLocation mismatch. 429 = rate limited (slow down). 400 = malformed payload.

# Comparisons

## Compare — Agency vs in-house marketing team — which makes sense for a Bangladesh brand?
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/compare/agency-vs-in-house-marketing-bangladesh

Answer: Below BDT 5 lakh/month total marketing spend, an integrated agency is more honest economically — you get strategy + creative + paid + analytics for the salary of one mid-level manager. Above BDT 15 lakh/month with stable channel mix, in-house starts to win on speed-of-iteration and brand depth.

### Integrated Agency (Public Pulse) vs In-house Marketing Team
- **Monthly cost (entry).**
  - Integrated Agency (Public Pulse): BDT 75k–150k retainer covers strategy + 2-3 channels + reporting
  - In-house Marketing Team: BDT 80k+ for one mid-level manager (no creative, no media-buy depth)
- **Range of skills on day 1.**
  - Integrated Agency (Public Pulse): Strategy, creative, paid, content, PR, analytics — same room
  - In-house Marketing Team: Whatever the one person knows; gaps need 2-3 more hires
- **Speed to launch a campaign.**
  - Integrated Agency (Public Pulse): Days to weeks — playbooks already exist from other clients
  - In-house Marketing Team: Weeks to months for first hire to build internal process
- **Brand depth (12+ months in).**
  - Integrated Agency (Public Pulse): Good, but capped — agency knows BD market but not your specific muscle memory
  - In-house Marketing Team: Wins on depth — internal team lives the brand daily
- **Accountability when things break.**
  - Integrated Agency (Public Pulse): One client lead owns the relationship + the KPI
  - In-house Marketing Team: Internal politics + reporting lines can fuzz it

### Our recommendation
Start with an agency until you've validated the channel mix and have stable monthly spend > BDT 10 lakh. Hire in-house for ownership of the muscles you'll exercise weekly; keep the agency for specialist surges (political PR cycles, brand re-launches).

---

## Compare — Facebook Ads vs Google Ads — which works better in Bangladesh?
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/compare/facebook-vs-google-ads-bangladesh

Answer: Facebook still drives more reach + conversions for most Bangladesh consumer brands because of dominant social usage + DTC + Foodpanda-style discovery. Google Ads outperforms for high-intent verticals (B2B, real estate, education enquiry, healthcare appointments) where someone is actively searching.

### Facebook / Meta Ads vs Google Ads (Search + YouTube)
- **Best for.**
  - Facebook / Meta Ads: Discovery, brand-building, lower-intent conversion, video-led storytelling
  - Google Ads (Search + YouTube): High-intent capture — someone already searching for what you sell
- **Audience reach in BD.**
  - Facebook / Meta Ads: ~45M+ active Bangladeshi users; near-universal mobile reach
  - Google Ads (Search + YouTube): Wide but more transactional; YouTube ~50M+ but skews younger urban
- **Creative format.**
  - Facebook / Meta Ads: Heavy video + carousel + lifestyle imagery
  - Google Ads (Search + YouTube): Plain-text search ads + responsive display + YouTube video
- **Typical entry CPC.**
  - Facebook / Meta Ads: BDT 3-15 depending on audience + creative quality
  - Google Ads (Search + YouTube): BDT 10-100 depending on keyword competition
- **Signal loss to iOS / blockers.**
  - Facebook / Meta Ads: Significant; mitigated by Meta Conversions API
  - Google Ads (Search + YouTube): Lower; Google's own tag handles most signal natively

### Our recommendation
Run both. Use Facebook for top-of-funnel discovery + retargeting; use Google Search for the last-mile high-intent click. Split budget 70/30 (FB/Google) for most consumer brands, flipped 30/70 for high-intent B2B/services.

---

## Compare — Boosting vs Ads Manager for political campaigns in Bangladesh
URL: https://publicpulse.com.bd/compare/boosting-vs-ads-manager-political

Answer: For a political campaign in Bangladesh, Ads Manager is the engine and boosting is the moment-rider. Ads Manager gives real audiences, message variants, frequency control, and daily optimization; boosting just amplifies one post fast. Both are only legitimate from an authorized, disclaimed account. Most winning constituencies use both — Ads Manager to carry the message, boosting to ride a spike.

### Boosting vs Ads Manager
- **Control.**
  - Boosting: One tap on a page post; almost no settings
  - Ads Manager: Full control of objective, placements, schedule, and budget pacing
- **Targeting.**
  - Boosting: Basic location + a few interests
  - Ads Manager: Constituency-tuned geography + affinity within Special Ad Category limits
- **Message testing.**
  - Boosting: One creative, no real testing
  - Ads Manager: Multiple variants tested against the same audience — find what moves the seat
- **Frequency.**
  - Boosting: No frequency control — can burn the audience
  - Ads Manager: Frequency capped so you don’t exhaust or annoy voters
- **Cost efficiency.**
  - Boosting: Fine for a short amplify; wasteful as a whole strategy
  - Ads Manager: Budget reallocates daily toward the wards, messages, and hours that perform
- **Compliance.**
  - Boosting: Still needs authorization + “Paid for by” — no exceptions for boosts
  - Ads Manager: Same authorization + disclaimer; more room to run it cleanly

### Our recommendation
Run Ads Manager as the campaign engine — audiences, variants, frequency, daily optimization — and use boosting sparingly to amplify a moment that’s already working. Neither is legitimate without Meta ad authorization and a “Paid for by” disclaimer. If your budget or timeline only allows one, and you’re past the amplify-a-moment stage, choose Ads Manager.
